props.gloss_en: R' Chanina of Sura: whether milk exempts [the next offspring from the firstborn] is the difference between R' Akiva and R' Yehoshua
milk exempts: an animal that has given milk -- its next offspring is not a firstborn
the ground for milk-exempts: follow the majority of animals, and most animals do not give milk unless they have given birth
milk does not exempt [the next offspring from the firstborn]
the ground for milk-does-not-exempt: there is a minority that give milk though they have not given birth
the presupposition of R' Chanina's account, as the stam states it at 20b.5: R' Yehoshua is concerned for a minority
the Yevamot mishna: if her mother-in-law [went overseas] she need not be concerned [that a levir was born]; if she left pregnant, she must be concerned
R' Yehoshua: even then she need not be concerned
R' Yehoshua's reason (ואמרינן): join the miscarrying minority to the females' half, the males are a minority -- and we are not concerned for a minority
rather, reverse: R' Yehoshua holds milk exempts and R' Akiva that it does not
the baraita: milk exempts -- the words of R' Yehoshua; R' Akiva says: milk does not exempt
the first tanna: a kid that bore three daughters, and each of her daughters bore three -- all of them enter the pen to be tithed
R' Shimon: I saw [such a kid] that yielded tithe within its year
(entertained) the tanna holds that an animal that expelled a discharge does not return and give birth within its year
even if an animal that expelled a discharge does return and give birth within its year, one that gave birth certainly does not -- so the mother cannot bear again alongside her daughters

ואמרינן: מאי טעמא דרבי יהושע? ...ולמיעוטא לא חיישינן -- the reason the Gemara gave for R' Yehoshua's ruling in Yevamot

objections.gloss_en: ומי חייש רבי יהושע למיעוט? והתנן: יצאה מליאה -- חוששת; רבי יהושע אומר: אינה חוששת, ואמרינן: ...ולמיעוטא לא חיישינן -- R' Yehoshua is NOT concerned for a minority. Conceded at 20b.7: אלא איפוך
